clue.text: Asian characters with bureaucrat seen struggling to comprehend European character

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the official and his jumbled companion enclose the Greek letter

parts.note: a mandarin is a high-ranking official, originally in imperial China

indicators.note: the letters of seen are thrashing about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, Greek being a European script

explanation.surface: An official battles to understand a foreign letter amid a page of Asian script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' jumbles the letters of 'seen', and 'to comprehend' wraps the bureaucrat-plus-jumble around the Greek letter, which lands at the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin Chinese is written in hanzi, the characters of the main language of China.

clue.text: Jazz band particularly inadequate — unconvincing style?

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz group

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: particularly means very, as in very good

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a jazz group's look as feeble and unconvincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' drops the last letter of VERY to give VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair swept across a bald patch rarely fools anyone, so the hairstyle is famously unconvincing.

clue.text: See 18
Grand very good price? Steep!

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, M in Roman numerals
ace is slang for excellent
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone balks at a fee of a thousand: very good, but what a steep price!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' reads as an exclamation about cost, but it is the verb meaning soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate food is to soften it by soaking in liquid, which is what steeping does.

clue.text: In shelter, stick vegetable

indicators.note: in places the gluey word within the sheltering word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
to gum is to stick something down

explanation.surface: A vegetable is stuck down somewhere under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils are the seeds and pods of plants of the pea family, eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Ready: set up to tackle Wimbledon's top seed

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so one piece holds the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to tune an instrument or engine is to set it right

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tennis player is ready and primed to take on the top seed at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TUNE to ENUT, which takes in W, the top of Wimbledon's. 'seed' is a tennis ranking in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is the kidney-shaped seed of a tropical tree, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Midnight mass's ending in dark and damp European city

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: dank means unpleasantly damp and gloomy

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Midnight mass ends somewhere dark and damp in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a large port city on the Baltic coast of Poland.

clue.text: Nervous: my old age pitiable — it was all so blissful once

definitions.text: it was all so blissful once

indicators.note: pitiable suggests something in a wretched state, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An anxious old person laments ageing, recalling how blissful everything once was.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the first idealised flush of romance, recalled fondly in later life.

clue.text: Trump's change of policy dealing with mug

parts.note: a book about something is dealing with it
mug is slang for the face

explanation.surface: A political U-turn by Trump concerns his own face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's' looks like the US president but is only part of the definition: any trump's reversal of policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete reversal of stance, like a soldier turning to face the other way.

clue.text: Enhance diet thus, originally in difficulty

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters within the other piece

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in without further ado

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A nutritionist suggests boosting a diet like this when it was first in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To add to something is to augment or improve it.

clue.text: Be off with Conservative deal — catastrophe!

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone urges walking away from a Tory agreement that is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco.

clue.text: Trouble in huge drunk guzzling last of gin

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so one piece takes in the other
drunk means in a disordered state, so the letters are jumbled
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble after drinking huge quantities of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN HUGE to UHINGE, and 'guzzling' places the final N of gin inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhinge someone is to unsettle or disturb their mind, a strong form of troubling.

clue.text: Prayer required to join Republican Party

indicators.note: being required to join means attached after, so the prayer follows the other piece

parts.note: Ave, short for Ave Maria, is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A prayer is needed before someone may join the Republican Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like the political Republican Party, but it is the definition for a lively gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large, lively party with dance music.

clue.text: System broken by main Irish party, open your eyes!

indicators.note: broken by means split open and filled, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a way is a method or system
key means chief or main
a wake is a gathering after a death, a famously Irish tradition

explanation.surface: A political system disrupted by Ireland's main party urges voters to open their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is a jocular call to rouse someone from sleep.

clue.text: Kansas gallery after painting

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece comes second

parts.note: Sunflowers is the famous series of paintings by Van Gogh
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain

explanation.surface: An exhibition in Kansas shows a gallery's collection after one painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Kansas's nickname comes from its wild sunflowers; the Tate is London's best-known gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nickname of the US state of Kansas, whose state flower is the wild sunflower.

clue.text: Feed hare the wrong way, true to form

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

indicators.note: to form means to shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Instructions to feed a hare wrongly, as is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns RUN into NUR; 'to form' rearranges TRUE as TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture a child or plant is to nourish and rear it.

clue.text: Vacuum-packed whiskey?

parts.note: whiskey is the radio code word for the letter W, and the word vacuum is packed with a pair of U letters, which is that letter's name

explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W, the letter whose name is the pair of U's found side by side inside 'vacuum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter W is named for its form as two U shapes joined, and its radio code word is whiskey.

clue.text: Tobacconist inhaling good quantity of muck

indicators.note: inhaling means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: Alfred Dunhill was a London tobacconist whose name became a cigarette and luxury brand

explanation.surface: A tobacconist inhales a good dose of filth.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNHILL is a British tobacco and luxury goods brand named after its founder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunghill is a heap of manure, a large pile of muck.

clue.text: Ludicrous, ultimately embarrassing and a slight con: UK — seen as this?

indicators.note: ludicrous means absurd and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
ultimately means at the end, so the word gives its last letter

explanation.surface: Something absurd and mildly fraudulent leaves the UK looking a figure of ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ludicrous' rearranges G (the end of embarrassing) with A SLIGHT CON UK. The whole clue also describes how a country so exposed would be viewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone seen as ludicrous and embarrassing is an object of public ridicule.

clue.text: On a trip in the air, as a jet-setter?

parts.note: someone on a drug trip is high
something in the air is flying

explanation.surface: A frequent traveller is airborne on yet another journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' suggests travel but means intoxicated, HIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, successful, globe-trotting person lives a glamorous, ambitious life.

clue.text: One's played God, unwittingly inspiring transgression and revolution, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of every one of these words

parts.words: God, unwittingly inspiring transgression and revolution

explanation.surface: Someone who played God unknowingly sparked sin and uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's played' looks like the start of 'One's played God', but it is the definition: something one plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a stringed instrument, something a musician plays.

clue.text: Beaten side latterly, with stuffing knocked out, surrenders

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
knocking the stuffing out of a word empties its middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A beaten team, demoralised towards the end, gives in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with stuffing knocked out' leaves LY from latterly; 'Beaten' rearranges SIDE with LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or submit, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Throw something in a brown envelope?

definitions.meaning: in British slang, to chuck something carelessly
a bribe, cash traditionally passed in a plain brown envelope

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means both to toss casually and a bribe.

clue.text: Chairman hugging companion, butch

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese communist leader
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A chairman embraces his comrade in a manly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone aggressively or showily masculine.

clue.text: Abominable feeling rejected, son taking time out

indicators.note: the son is taken in as a replacement
the time letter is put out to make room
rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling

explanation.surface: A son, feeling rejected, takes time out, which is abominable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns EMOTION into NOITOME; 'taking' and 'out' swap its T for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially in smell.

clue.text: Purplish-pink haze initially obstructing sun, say?

indicators.note: obstructing means blocking, so the letter sits within the other piece

parts.note: the sun is an example of a heater, warming the earth

indicators.note: initially means at the start, giving the first letter

explanation.surface: A purplish-pink haze at first blocks out the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a pale purple colour, named after the moorland plant's flowers.

clue.text: See 15
Rock hid alpine plants

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alpine plants are tucked away among rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a rockery noun beside alpine plants, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphiniums, also called larkspurs, are tall garden plants with spikes of blue flowers.
